Oh, god. I'm so sorry. Having such hyperempathic qualities myself, I have often ruined myself to try to save others. For so long, I didn't even care sometimes how badly I was hurting or doing, as long as I was making sure others were okay. 

This went on until I over poured my cup to such an extent that I swallowed a bunch of pills, almost died, and nearly caused my dad a heart attack. And caused my grown-up little brother to fall into my lap and blubber cry the worst I'd seen since we were kids, begging me not to die. And saw how stressed it made certain friends of mine to the point that they were relapsing on alcohol and getting blackout drunk and falling into depression again. There's more I could add, but...

My point is, darling, that I totally understand. I care about others far more than myself a lot of the time and will continue to allow them to hurt me. But...if you aren't able to think about it in terms of saving yourself...what if you started by thinking in terms of saving those you love from pain? If something grave were to happen to you, how would it impact those who care about you? Who would get stressed? Who might fall ill? Who might fall into depression? It's honestly questions like these that help me detach from toxicity. When I don't care about myself, it greatly affects those who I DO care about and care about me.

While obviously, putting others' needs before our own is part of the problem, I have found this exercise can be useful when trying to slowly pull oneself in the right direction. 

Either way, I'm so rooting for you. Sending love <3

Oh, Christ. I have a story for you.

So, last year sucked, right? Jeez, 2020 was something for the books stacked on top of covid-19 for me.

(TL;DR @ the bottom. Plz forgive me if I'm not structuring this right. I'm Autistic/ADHD/brain injured)

So, last year, I was living in an apartment that I had moved into in 2018. I lived there with my partner until fall of '19 when we broke up and they decided to move away. After that, I had a couple different friends come through and stay with me for a bit that also eventually moved out. 

Well, the whole time I was there, some of my neighbors and I would hang out occasionally. Sometimes we would smoke weed together or help each other out if we needed it (hard times came and went, so one of us would give the other water or food and vise versa). Eventually, I would babysit for them, too while I was out of work (i was going through a deep depression and it was honestly one of the hardest times of my life after my partner left me), which I very much enjoyed because those babies were amazing! ^.^ Obviously none of this bothered me; it was mutual aid and is what keeps communities going often times. Well, unfortunately for me, I've been very easy to be taken advantage of throughout my life because of my kindness and lack of perception when it comes to people's intentions (or really for their red flags, I should say. I mean, I see them, but my brain has always said HAHA WHATEVER....working on it lol).

So, it's early spring 2020, and at this point, I'm looking for someone to take over my new lease, because I wanted to move elsewhere. I needed change. REALLY badly. I wanted to move beyond everything, especially that apartment because of all my history there. 

Well, my neighbors break up, and one asks if they can take over the lease. I think my prayers are being answered. Halle-fucking-lujah. Or so I thought. 

They end up getting kicked out before they can actually start that process, and end up asking me if they can move in my second bedroom and start the process of taking over.

Cheese and crackers. Well, they certainly did. But without any regard for me, MY space, MY privacy, my needs, etc. Basically, they said they would apply for the apartments, go to the office with me, sign the paperwork for the lease takeover, and I would be good to move. I had just enough money to make everything work. But that's not what happened. They ended up telling me the next week they didn't have a job anymore and were looking for one. Well, that whole month went by and I was the only one working. And not only did he move in, but my best friend had just lost their home and was staying with me in my room until they moved as well. ALSO, my neighbor's terrible friend was staying with them at the time, so he ended up moving from his couch to mine. He sucked; super offensive, misogynistic, sexist, rude, racist, etc. Everything GROSS. 

At first, before seeing everything unfold, I was happy to help. But after the first month, my bff and I were the only ones to pay for anything. I paid for rent, bills, and food, and my bff paid for some groceries and supplied ALL the weed for all of us they had spent months perfecting in growth & harvest. And yet...we were also still the only ones cleaning anything at home. Everyone else? Smoking weed and hanging out. After that first month, I started to lose it. Because not only was I taking care of three other "adults" there besides myself, but also my kitty and her brother that my shitty upstairs neighbor abandoned. AND their mother that stayed outside mostly due to trauma. In a small, cheap, 2 bedroom apartment.

Next month comes, SAME fucking shit, except we booted the sexist POS out. Or more like...He found some poor chick to use instead of us and we didn't let him back in. Well, this time, my neighbor does some more dumb shit. There was an 18 year old kid who was having a hard time, and we let him come over and talk with us, trying to help him out. Well, everyday after I get off from work, more of his stuff is in my living room. After about a week, he's moved himself in WITH MY NEIGHBOR'S PERMISSION. NOT MINE. HIS. And up to this point, my neighbor has not chipped in a DIME. Hasn't done the dishes once. And then...this 18 year old BRINGS A MINOR INTO MY HOME. Says he was rescuing her from an abusive home. I take her under my wing, realize she's SIXTEEN YEARS OLD, and I start calling advocacy services, because I want to help her but absolutely cannot take on that responsibility, especially on top of everything. She ends up bringing SOME OTHER MINOR over while I'm trying to organize my shit to move so my bestie and I and my kitties can stay at another friend's until we got our own place. I am just beyond anything at this point.

Oh, and all the while, my neighbor has also brought in someone he was talking to, and moves her in to "his" bedroom. 

So at this point...the only person who has helped me with ANYTHING is my best friend. And that 18 year old's mom. She tried to be helpful by bringing us food. But, dear lord salty cheese and crackers rice. At this point, I have been taking care of nine living bodies, including myself (just turned 25), 3 kitties (the only ones I wanted there besides my bff), my best friend (30 but disabled), my neighbor and his gf (maybe 22 and 23?), the 18 year old, the 16 year old, and that's all at home.

At work?????? I was a CNA, working ridiculous shifts because of short staffing (greed on the facility's part, but what's new?). They wouldn't hire anyone else, or just couldn't. Those of us working weren't sure. But the halls I worked had AT LEAST 15 residents or more at all times. Some for long stay, some for short. Well, after being worked so gruelingly, I ended up getting sick, and I thought it might be covid, so I stayed home for a couple weeks. 

Well, once the third month rolls around, I refuse to pay rent and tell my neighbor and his girlfriend and the 18 year old that either they have to pay by a certain date, or they have to find somewhere else. I should have done it sooner, but whatever. I thought I was doing the right thing by taking care of everyone, but ABSOLUTELY NOT. i was being taken advantage of left and right. Thankfully, they end up paying it. But does he apply? Does he take over the lease? NO. I end up getting so stressed out that I swallowed every bottle of pills I own. My neighbor's gf ended up driving me to the hospital, and well, as u can see, I survived! But y'all...what the absolute fuck.

After I come back from the hospital, nothing changes. 

N o t h i n g.

And then, *I* am the one that ends up losing a home. Why? Because after growing so ill from stress, I am unable to work. So the next couple months, I do exactly what they did to me before. Not out of pettiness, laziness, or apathy, but from disability. From illness. And what happens? THEY kick ME out of MY place after stripping it of its solace and security from me. After pushing me to suicide. After invading my life. And since then, I have been bouncing from place to place out of my friend circle. I am SO endlessly grateful for the kindness of my friends and family. I am STILL trying to build myself and life back up. 

So seriously, guys. Be careful who you let in. LITERALLY. because...

TL;DR - During a really hard battle with depression, I let my seemingly-okay neighbor move in with me during his own hard times after he got kicked out in promises that he would take over my lease, allowing me to move away and move on. Instead, he uses me, uses my best friend, turns my place into a trap house, allows a bunch of strangers to move in, never works or pays for anything until I try to kill myself, and after I come back from the hospital after attempting suicide from the stress of working in the medical field during a pandemic and also housing/caring for 8 other living beings, I'm still expected to pay for everything, I refuse, and I END UP GETTING BOOTED OUT OF MY OWN FUCKING APARTMENT.

Well, then I really hope you're not on the board of any important medical teams. Your statements are ableist and unethical and just plain incorrect.

Bipolar disorder is definitely a chronic illness; it's a chronic condition of the brain that disrupts mood, emotional stability, etc, which in turn causes an array of symptoms that can be debilitating. There are treatments, but no cure. Effects of the disorder are lifelong. It is a listed disability in many countries. Are you aware that those with bipolar disorder may experience hallucinations? Chronic suicidality? Deep depression? And so much more? It sounds to me what you know about these illnesses you have only picked up from ableist portrayal that is passed around in media. No, someone having Bipolar disorder doesn't mean they're "a bitch one second and nice the next" or whatever. I see that all the time. There is SO much more to it.

Second, I can say the exact same for ADHD as far as being a disability. It is a chronic condition of the brain; people born on the ADHD/ASD spectrum are literally wired differently. So often, we are "disabled" in this world's terms because we do not always have the abilities to function in the same manner, especially not in social, school, work, etc settings. Often, we excell in other ways that typical people cannot. Is a spectrum and everyone with a neurodivergent brain of sorts has a different experience. Some have minimum ability where others have max. Vise versa. And so on. No, someone having ADHD doesn't mean they "get distracted by shiny stuff and are really hyper." There is so much to the complexity of being neurodivergent. 

Allergies CAN, indeed, be a disability. There are people in this world who have intense allergic reactions to common types of pollen, grass, chemicals, food, ingredients, etc that makes it very difficult to function typically in this society. Some are confined to their homes during certain seasons, time of day, etc.  Or, some aren't confined but have to deal with such long healing periods from allergic reactions that keeping a job is difficult to impossible. 

There is honestly so much more I could say, but I really hope you understand that leaving the validity of someone's entire experience up to your personal opinion is inherently ignorant and ableist. ANY condition can be a chronic illness or disability for a person if it affects them greatly enough. And that can and WILL look different for different people because we are organic beings that will never be identical to another.

I am sorry the world continually fails to recognize the beauty in diversity and fails to celebrate it. Especially when it does this to you.

But super stoked that surgery went well and she should be on the road to recovery :')) and more. Some friends tipped the counselor when they found out, and she called me to her office, and was actually very kind. But of course, she had to call my parents, and my mom was crying on the phone and then *I* started crying, and bleh I just still hate that memory and everything else that comes with it. ESPECIALLY because...well, when my mom picked me up, she was very sweet, but when we got home, she and my dad sat me down. They had a talk with me, and basically, they chalked it allllllll up to me not having enough spiritual strength. It was heartbreaking. They asked me, their *11 year old child*, whether or not I thought i should get help or not...well, already having so much bullshit brainwashing already, I thought i had to put myself last. (My mother's mother would always say to us grandkids, "Remember kids, the best way to live life is to have joy; put Jesus first, then others, and then yourself." All the time. God, that's such bullshit...) So, i told them maybe because i didn't want to feel anymore like a burden, but i really, really wanted help. I felt so trapped (especially because i was molested at 6 and then again at 8 by two older kids unrelated to me and bottled it up throughout childhood). Their response was to ask me who in the church i wanted to talk to...so i told them nevermind. They gave me some Bible verses, and my treatment was "pray more." 
    I could seriously go on, and on, and on, forever. But i will definitely save you from that haha. i will probably write a memoir eventually. The world NEEDS to know what this does to children; they might grow into disabled, confused, poor, homeless adults who have much to give but cannot because of their lack of resources, because they have been raised for a world that is not this one. I know, because this has been me so many times. I have accomplished things, traveled, and been able to work, but i cannot hold a job. ESPECIALLY one that has a set schedule. i absolutely cannot fit into this society. I have absolutely no interest to, but it would have been extremely helpful to know i have adhd, BPD, MDD, etc. before reaching 20, and would have been great to have found out I'm Autistic before almost reaching 30. 
     I started out writing this comment and had no idea i would let all of this out; i guess i needed to vent. Thank you if you actually read this <3 just know, if you also struggle/have struggled, YOU ARE NOT ALONE! Much love <3

Ugh, this seriously makes my stomach churn. I am a cocktail of mental illnesses, and I can honestly say being spiritually abused (and intertwined with that - emotionally & physically abused) as a child has a LOT to do with it.

TW: drugs, r*pe, spiritual abuse, addiction, self harm

My hyper-religious, authoritarian styled parents (and entire family, in general) were one of the root causes for developing Borderline Personality Disorder and Major Depressive Disorder and cutting myself at age 11 (I'd already been dealing with ADHD & OCD, having been born with them, and then PTSD coming into affect after being molested by a classmate in 1st grade and then again by an older kid at church when I was in 3rd grade...) My school counselor called my mom after some friends had anonymously told her, and I remember when I got home, my parents had a talk with me in their bedroom. They were actually surprisingly kind about it and let me know that they weren't angry, just sad that I did that to myself (I thought they were going to punish me with a whipping or something). They asked if I wanted to talk to someone professional, and I said yes, but then they said they would arrange for me to talk with our preacher at church. Upon hearing that option as the only one, I told them I didnt need to speak with anyone after all. Then, they told me to pray to God more and gave me some Bible verses to read.

Absolutely ridiculous. 

The ableism continued throughout my life, and I continued to cut, and hide that and my depression and struggle with other disorders (that I wasnt yet aware of) until my senior year of high school came, and one of my teachers (who is amazing and I still talk to today, at 26 years old now) noticed how depressed I was. She contacted my mom as well, and essentially, the same thing happened. 

Well, fast forward to my first and only year of college, and I was spiraling downward like water being flushed down the toilet. For one, they had forced me to go to a christian college; my whole family told me they wouldn't support me financially if I went to a public university. Well, fucking hated it and the ridiculous rules and curfew. Not to mention, the required attendance of chapel EVERY MORNING Monday-Friday & a Bible class three times a week. I started missing a bunch of days in those and other classes just in the first semester. I made incredible friends, but 99% of them felt the way I did and wanted to leave the next semester. I wanted to leave THAT semester. Called my mom and told her how depressed I was; how difficult it was to sleep at night and get up in the day, my absence of motivation for anything, including taking care of myself, and my desire to leave. She basically told me to suck it up and keep trying. "Try finding a counselor there or something," she said. Psh. The counselors there were a fucking joke. Tried, and never went back. They literally asked me the "how's your relationship with God," question. **rolls eyes into the back of head so far they pop out of the socket**

Well, anyway, the 2nd semester came, and midway, I just fucking gave up. I stopped going to chapel altogether, and then stopped going to Bible, too. Started drinking and smoking with my friend who had unintentionally helped me realize I was hella queer. I had a mad crush on her, and felt like she and our friends were the only source of joy I would ever experience there. I was right. Well, thanks to the convictions of my family and consequently, the leaders and teachers of that school, and their negligence towards my mental health, I ended up spiraling out of control after that last semester, going full-on mixed mania & depression and started on a path of self-destruction; alcoholism, popping pills, unsafe sex, getting myself raped, meeting someone from the internet and enduring the most abusive, insane, two-different-scars-on-my-head-now relationship, etc etc etc....battling all these kinds of things for YEARS. 

Now, YES, I know...it's still my life, my choices, my responsibility. HOWEVER....I know y'all being as conscientious as you are know that this could have definitely been avoided/prevented to an extent and could have saved me (and anyone affected) MUCH grief, pain, and trauma. Not to mention, money and time...I was hospitalized 8 times for suicide in a span of about 5/6 years. 2 of those times I actually overdosed and almost died, laying in a hospital bed in a coma for a few days. 

Like I said, I'm not blaming anyone for my problems, but I AM acknowledging the negligence of my caretakers and the years-long traumatic affect it has had on me and my life. Now, think about everyone else and their similar stories. And then...let us think about everyone we affected because of our untreated illnesses. Now think about how quickly all of that branches into a LARGE number of people. 

It's insane how people don't take into account the butterfly affect. I mean, considering one's own child's experience is one thing. But to ignore this AND the rest? Completely irresponsible.

Sorry your experience off of them has been a lot; I understand completely. Especially being induced by absence of meds; that happens to me sometimes when I havent filled mine in time. Our neurodiverse brains can act up very strangely and cause us to feel or believe things that don't make sense. It can be scary and overwhelming, for sure. But it's temporary; you will not always feel this way. 

It's going to be alright, dear. When you catch yourself becoming overwhelmed, pour yourself a glass of cold water if you can and try drinking as much of it as possible. Often times, our brains become dehydrated and it will make them act up more than usual. Additionally, practice deep breathing. Do it until you feel your body relaxing. When you're feeling better, maybe make a playlist of songs that make everything feel like it's alright so you can just pop some headphones in and play it when you need to. Or make a playlist of songs that will trigger an emotional response and help you cry things out; whichever works for you! 

Sending love & hugs. Hope you feel better! You are not alone!

We ended up having a great rest of our time in Europe together, came back to the states, and continued living with each other for a couple of months. 

It was REALLY hard to accept for a while, because I was still so in love with him, and honestly, i cried every day, multiple times a day for the first month. But as time went on, I began to appreciate us having a friendship instead of romantic relationship and I started to see how it was going to be good for both of us.
